page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The Interview
title: The Interview
description:
Tip Top Trading is the fastest-growing company in the plastic fruit sector, and Anna desperately wants to be a part of it. Her job interview for a position in sales is going to be a challenge. How will she cope?
This programme focuses on useful language for job interviews.
phrases: A good example that comes to mind…

listening_challenge.question: What was Anna's role in the university debating society?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hold tight please! This is Anna, on a bus going to an interview for a job as a sales executive at Tip Top Trading – one of London's fastest growing companies. How are you feeling Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, a little nervous but I really want this job.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well don't worry Anna, as long as you say the right things, you'll be fine.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: The right things!? Like what?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You need to sell yourself, be confident, not arrogant and give examples. Like: A good example that comes to mind. I'm particularly proud of. Timekeeping is important to me.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right. Thanks. Perhaps you can come with me?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Sorry Anna, you're on your own now – but we'll be listening in. Look! You've just arrived. Good luck!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Come in. Hello, I'm Paul, the Manager of Tip Top Trading. And you must be….?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It's Anna.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, very good. Thanks for coming. Now somewhere in this pile, I've got your CV…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, is that it there?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh yes, thanks Hannah. Your qualifications look impressive but what sales experience can you bring to our company?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I worked in a shop once.
Narrator: Ohhh Anna! Sell yourself. Give a good example!
Anna: Oh right…mmm….well a good example that comes to mind is when I was involved with a campaign to promote and sell a new range of clothes – I loved doing it and it was…
Denise: Oh sorry, excuse me, here's your tea Paul.
Paul: Thanks Denise. Now Anna, it looks like you've achieved a lot during your time at university. Could you give me an example of good team working during your time there?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Sorry! I forgot the sugar.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Thank you Denise.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hmm, so you want an example? I was the treasurer of the debating society at university. That was OK I suppose.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Come on Anna. Be more enthusiastic – the debating society is exciting!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I mean… I'm particularly proud of how I organised the finances for the debating society. We had a very small budget and I had to make decisions on what to buy.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: I like it! "I'm particularly proud of" - Positive but not boasting. You're doing well.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Very impressive – so you're a good planner Anna! We like organised people here... ooops, silly me. I seemed to have spilt tea over your CV.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, do you need some help?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh no…I'm sure it'll dry out… carry on please…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Also… timekeeping is important to me…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: "Timekeeping is important to me" – that's good!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I always try to complete my work on time. At university I never handed my assignments in late.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: That's good to hear. We like punctuality here…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Excuse me Paul. Sorry it's a bit late – but I thought you might like a biscuit with your tea.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hmm thanks….oh lovely, custard creams… mmm. Now Hannah, finally I wanted to ask you what exactly made you apply for this job at this company?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Errrr… ooo… well. The reason I applied is….

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes, yes, yes Anna? Do you need a bit more time to think?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Errr…mmm…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What's she going to say? How would you answer that? Join us next time to find out. Before we go, here's a reminder of some of the great lines Anna's used today… A good example that comes to mind I'm particularly proud of. Timekeeping is important to me. Until next time, bye bye! ·
